description: Capability for the main window. NOTE on the externalBin sidecars (`myne`, `myne-tor`): neither is launched from the webview, so neither gets a permission here. `myne` is run by the user from a terminal; `myne-tor` (arti, MYND-650) is spawned host-side by Rust when the device-local Tor routing option is on. A Tauri capability grants the WEBVIEW an IPC surface — so adding `shell:allow-execute` (or any process-spawn permission) would let page-context code choose WHICH program runs, which is the thing to refuse. Note the distinction, because the sync bundle already grants something adjacent: `sync:allow-sync-set-tor-routing` does start `myne-tor`, but the webview supplies one boolean — the executable path and the argv are both resolved host-side and neither is user-supplied. Both start a process; only `shell:` lets the caller pick it. The recorded argument, and the guard that notices a second one appearing, are `no_egress::IN_APP_PROCESS_SPAWN_PERMISSIONS`. If you came here to add a `shell:`/`process:` permission: don't; the launch belongs in the host lifecycle module. NOTE on `opener` (myne#385): `reveal_item_in_dir` is granted by `opener:default` and is NOT listed again on its own — a second identifier for a command already in the bundle resolves to the same authorization set, so it reads as a decision without being one. It also cannot be scoped: the upstream command consults no `CommandScope`/`GlobalScope`, so an `allow` array beside it would be ignored at runtime. Its production consumers are the page-side `revealItemInDir` call sites: the model path panel's reveal button (`src/components/settings/AiPanel.tsx`), the vault-export summary's "Show in folder" (`src/components/export/VaultExportModal.tsx`) and the note-export toast's "Show in folder" action (`src/notes/exportFlow.ts`). `diagnostics|reveal_logs_folder` (myne#860) does not consume the grant: it calls the Rust opener API host-side (`app.opener().reveal_item_in_dir(...)`) on a directory it resolves itself, so narrowing `opener:default` is unaffected by it. NOTE on `core` (myne#384): the three `core:*:default` entries are enumerated rather than taken as the `core:default` bundle, which resolved to 92 command grants where 40 are reachable from the platform seam. The five dropped sub-defaults — `core:menu`, `core:tray`, `core:app`, `core:image`, `core:webview` and `core:resources` — have no consumer on either idiom (typed `@tauri-apps/api/*` import or raw `plugin:<x>|<y>` literal), but `core:menu`'s 22 handlers are registered unconditionally on desktop, so the grant let page context install its own application menu. Add a sub-default back only with a named consumer; `no_egress::GRANTED_CORE_NAMESPACES` is the roster that notices either direction of drift.
